newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco banks expect new forex trading freedom.
newsitem.headline: Morocco banks expect new forex trading freedom.

text.p: Moroccan bankers expect the central bank, Banque al-Maghrib, soon to allow them to trade on the international spot market for the first time, to sell or buy any currency.
Chief dealer Mohamed Najib Lazrak with the Banque Morocaine du Commerce Exterieur (BMCE) told Reuters on Monday the decision was expected soon and would improve competition and liquidity.
"Now, we have to go through the central bank or on the domestic market. This is very difficult. All the market is usually one way -- long in dollars or French francs, for example.
"This change will enable us to go on the international market to sell and buy any currency. We need this," he said.
Ali Benani, director of Wafabank's trading room, told Reuters: "Banks will be able to have access to foreign currency against foreign currency at a better cost.
"A bank will be able to get rid of a foreign currency it does not need on the international market at a better rate than that available on the local market, and vice versa."
A spokesman for the Banque al-Maghrib said on Monday: "The decision has not been taken yet."
One banker said that the change would also mean that banks would have to learn fully to take on the risks of volatility in the international foreign exchange market.
Commercial bankers said the change could help importers and exporters who have to pay a fee on currency purchases.
